principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization; only change the launch boundary that blocks real Cell 03 progress.
Do not use arbitrary pre-run dollar guesses as correctness gates.
Keep provider execution evidence distinct from authorization-envelope evidence.
Keep estimates, provider-reported usage, and derived cost mechanically separate.
Preserve Cell 03-only scope and keep later cells blocked.
drivers: The user explicitly rejected manual budget guessing and wants actual spend calculated after task execution.
Provider calls must not be made from this authorization story; the story can only prepare a bounded execution envelope.
Existing artifacts and checker currently assume missing budget fields keep provider execution disabled, so the state model must be updated carefully.

options.name: Keep dollar hard cap as launch gate
pros: Matches the old B-c25c guardrail wording
cons: Forces the user to guess a budget before knowing actual cost
Does not match the new user requirement
Can block legitimate Cell 03 progress for an arbitrary number

options.name: Remove all budget and execution limits
pros: No budget prompt to the user
cons: Allows unbounded retry or token loops

options.name: Use frozen execution envelope plus postflight usage accounting
pros: Bounds execution by scope, rows, retries, timeout, and token/output limits
Keeps actual provider usage as postflight truth
cons: Does not itself run provider calls
Requires a later execution step to consume the envelope

chosen: Use frozen execution envelope plus postflight usage accounting
rationale: This matches the user correction while preserving correctness: Cell 03 can be prepared for real execution without using an arbitrary pre-run dollar amount as the gate, and actual spend is recorded after execution from provider-reported usage.

preMortem.scenario: The envelope accidentally enables provider calls from this story.
preMortem.trigger: providerCallEnabled or result rows are set true in B-6529 artifacts.
preMortem.consequence: Authorization evidence is confused with execution evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker must assert provider calls from this authorization story remain disabled and no outcome rows exist.

preMortem.scenario: Dollar cap is removed but retry/token/time bounds are also missing.
preMortem.trigger: Execution envelope omits maxRetries, timeout, or token/output limits.
preMortem.consequence: The future provider execution can run unbounded even without a dollar cap.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker must require execution bounds and reject unbounded retry loops.

preMortem.scenario: Estimate is treated as final usage.
preMortem.trigger: Usage accounting policy merges preflight estimates with provider-reported final usage.
preMortem.consequence: Cost comparison becomes misleading and paper evidence can overclaim.
preMortem.mitigation: Policy and checker must keep estimate, provider-reported usage, and derived cost fields separate.

preMortem.trigger: Cell 06 or other cell state changes during Cell 03 envelope work.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker keeps Cell 06 blocked and rejects Cell 02/04/Phase 2 authorization in this story.
